title: Jellyfish blooms: their costs and suspected causes

sources.title: Massive Outbreak of Jellyfish Could Spell Trouble for Fisheries
The upside of rising jellyfish numbers? Many animals eat them

sources.publisher: University of Alaska Fairbanks Sea Grant (NOSB)
sources.title: Research Project for the 2011 Alaska Region National Ocean Sciences Bowl
sources.note: 只取「水母破壞漁網、壓壞或螫傷漁獲」這一點

facts.text: Huge jellyfish blooms have filled and torn fishing nets, for example in Japan, crushing or stinging the fish caught in them.
Blooms also invade fish farms, block cooling-water intakes at coastal power plants and force beaches to close.
Overfishing may help jellyfish by removing fish that compete with them for food or eat them.
Farm and city runoff feeds algae; as they decay, low-oxygen zones form that fish avoid but jellyfish tolerate.
Warmer seas may help some jellyfish grow and spread.
Jellyfish begin life as polyps attached to hard surfaces; piers, platforms and sea walls may give polyps more places to settle.
Scientists disagree on whether blooms are rising worldwide; blooms have occurred throughout history and populations naturally rise and fall.
Leatherback sea turtles feed almost entirely on jellyfish.
Some kinds of jellyfish are eaten as food in China, Japan and other Asian countries.
